learner_operation: Identify upper or lower triangular square matrices by checking every entry on the specified side of the main diagonal.

fixed_features.feature: Square matrices and upper/lower zero test
fixed_features.justification: Lesson Introduction defines both triangular types by all entries strictly on one side of the diagonal being zero.

fixed_features.feature: One qualifying matrix in easy five-choice radio bank
fixed_features.justification: All supplied easy prompts ask for one matrix. Maintaining this cardinality preserves the response contract.

answer_roles.role: Qualifying label and its displayed position
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Any A-E matrix can qualify with the same square shape and exactly-one constraint; update solution and keys from classification.
answer_roles.observed: Each easy source profile permanently assigns its qualifying label. Labels are recoverable from dimension tuples even after option shuffles.

answer_roles.role: Candidate dimensions and forbidden/allowed support counts
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Within 2x2/3x3 easy workload, swap eligible roles, zero patterns and targets without retaining a source label assignment.
answer_roles.observed: Source-profile per-label dimensions and support counts are enforced; minimal role-swap is rejected.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Upper/lower changes prompt, inspected side, matrix support and explanation together.
answer_roles.observed: Both orientations sampled; transpose pair has correct visible statements, math and native grading.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Any in-bound diagonal value preserves membership.
answer_roles.observed: Controlled diagonal change accepted, response preserved, rendered value updates.

coverage.case: Every supported easy profile, two target orientations and independently computed correct matrix
coverage.result: 72 easy records, 12 per profile; correct labels remain fixed by profile. Both upper and lower occur.
8 of 13 replay at source parameters; 5 current profiles are rejected, including two easy banks.

coverage.case: Exact runner batch after deduplication and difficulty filtering
coverage.result: 5 of 5 accepted; size-only strategy succeeds on all 5.

counterfactuals.change: Swap complete A and E matrices in q-126354, seed 20261022, holding target, bank size, entries, 2x2 shapes and exactly-one membership constant.
counterfactuals.expected: A becomes sole qualifying matrix; solution and native grader must follow changed membership.
counterfactuals.observed: Generator rejects before rendering/grading: complete profile support counts must be preserved. The after-side cannot be rendered or graded because the generator refuses to produce it.
counterfactuals.justification: The source definition assigns no special property to labels; swapping equally sized matrices preserves the intended skill and workload.

counterfactuals.change: Reverse upper/lower target and transpose every matrix, retaining other values and names.
counterfactuals.expected: Inspected side and prose reverse; E remains the correct label by transposition equivalence.
counterfactuals.observed: Before/after visible mathematics and solution inspected; native grader accepts E and rejects all other choices for both records. Actual UI screenshots show changed target and matrices.
counterfactuals.justification: Directly tests dependence on the lesson upper/lower distinction with a valid matched pair.

counterfactuals.change: Change E(1,1) only to 11 (or -11 if it was 11).
counterfactuals.expected: E remains the sole qualifying matrix; prompt target and classification explanation preserve membership.
counterfactuals.observed: Accepted; displayed matrix and worked solution reflect new diagonal, independent predicate and native grading preserve the same response.
counterfactuals.justification: Introduction explicitly permits any number including zero on the diagonal.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Choose A alone for A=4x4; otherwise choose A and B (all three 2x2).

shortcut_probes.strategy: Always select the matrix labeled D; ignore every entry and its size.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: All five records use q-126352 and have correct label D. Uniform random choice among five is 0.2. This perfect fixed-label shortcut affects the actual batch even though larger control sets contain other correct labels.

stages_examined: learner difficulty-band selection and history exclusion rules
delivery.result: 72/72 control and 5/5 batch survive, preserving perfect dimension-only prediction. A faithful single-easy-band engine selection reproduction retains the cue in every draw, and removal of previously seen questions cannot defeat a rule valid for each remaining generated record. Live policy weights/history were not supplied; conclusions are conditional on this generated easy pool.

limitations: No finite audit establishes absence of every shortcut. This audit demonstrates a specific universal dimension-signature shortcut for the current six-profile easy domain.
Five current source profiles cannot be replayed.
Relevant role-change counterfactual cannot reach rendering/grading because the generator rejects legitimate parameters.
Historical generation seeds are not captured; inventory records use exact content reconstruction and explicit captured ID bindings.
Live policy configuration, learner histories and later inventory changes are outside the captured snapshot.
